challenge.name: The Consent Gap
challenge.description: A new model version requires loyalty basket data, but the deployment pipeline lacks the governance controls to verify consent. #automation_alex# wants to push the automated deployment forward immediately to meet the promotion deadline, while #requirements_reuben# insists on a manual review process to ensure legal compliance. #automation_alex# is open to adding a manual approval step if it keeps the pipeline moving, but #requirements_reuben# will not accept any automated path without full audit trails.

output.content: The promotion leaflet goes to print in nine days, so we cannot afford a full two week validation cycle for the new loyalty feature. If the shadow test runs clean for three consecutive nights and matches the live forecast within acceptable error margins, I am willing to skip the canary deployment phase entirely. We accept the risk of a slightly less stable rollout in exchange for hitting the middle aisle allocation deadline. This trade off lets us use the saved time to focus on verifying the consent flags in the data pipeline, which is where the real legal exposure sits. We need to ship the model by Friday to keep the weekly promotion calendar on track.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly states that the team is accepting the risk of a less stable rollout in exchange for meeting the deadline, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
